spans.text: Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of readers, writers and readers can run at the same time.
Readers bypass the main file’s write locks by reconstructing their snapshot from the WAL, which is what enables true concurrent read/write isolation.
TL;DR— Tuning the write‑ahead log (WAL) can increase transaction throughput by 2‑3× without sacrificing durability.

Write transactions are very fast since they only involve writing
the content once (versus twice for rollback-journal transactions)
and because the writes are all sequential.

claims.text: WAL mode allows independent read snapshots to coexist with active writes to the log, eliminating the lock contention that forces readers and writers to serialize through a single file in rollback journaling. This architectural change means your database can sustain more simultaneous users without transaction delays.

meta.query: What concurrent read-write throughput improvements do independent benchmarks measure when using write-ahead logging instead of rollback journaling, and how do these improvements vary across different database sizes and concurrency levels?
meta.capability: You can support higher concurrent user loads by enabling simultaneous read and write operations without mutual blocking.

claims.text: WAL configurations can achieve 2-3x transaction throughput improvement by optimizing buffer size, sync policy, checkpoint frequency, and hardware settings like memory-mapped I/O, allowing additional capacity extraction from existing infrastructure before provisioning new database nodes. This multiplier applies to the same hardware; configuration changes precede purchasing decisions.

claims.text: WAL writes committed transactions once sequentially to the log file, whereas rollback journaling writes original page content to the journal then writes changes to the database file. This one-versus-two write architecture reduces per-transaction disk I/O and eliminates the sequential write burden that would be required in dual-pass modes.
